papers.title: OvisOCR2 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Abstract  We introduce OvisOCR2, a 0.8B document parsing model. OvisOCR2 is designed as an end-to-end parser: given a document page image, it generates a Markdown representation in natural reading order, covering text, formulas, tables, and visual regions. We build a data engine that combines filtered real-document annotations with synthetic pages whose rendered images and Markdown targets are derived from the same HTML source. The training recipe includes supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning on a 4B branch with a multi-component reward design, on-policy distillation into the 0.8B model, and model fusion. On OmniDocBench v1.6, OvisOCR2 achieves a state-of-the-art overall score of 96.58, placing an end-to-end model at the top of this leaderboard previously dominated by pipeline methods and highlighting the potential of end-to-end document parsing. On PureDocBench, OvisOCR2 also achieves the highest Avg3 score of 75.06. Beyond these two public benchmarks, we evaluate OvisOCR2 on an in-house benchmark designed to cover a broader set of long-tail and challenging scenarios. OvisOCR2 obtains the best overall performance among the compared methods, providing further evidence of its generalization and robustness. OvisOCR2 is available at https://huggingface.co/ATH-MaaS/OvisOCR2.

ru.title: OvisOCR2: Новая эра парсинга документов
ru.desc: OvisOCR2 — это модель парсинга документов с 0.8 миллиарда параметров. Она работает как конечный парсер, который принимает изображение страницы документа и генерирует представление в формате Markdown. Модель была обучена с использованием смешанных данных, включая реальные аннотации и синтетические страницы, а также использует обучение с подкреплением. OvisOCR2 показывает превосходные результаты на различных бенчмарках, устанавливая новые достижения для end-to-end парсинга документов.

en.title: Revolutionizing Document Parsing with OvisOCR2
en.desc: OvisOCR2 is a document parsing model that processes images of documents and converts them into a structured Markdown format. It uses a combination of real and synthetic data for training, employing techniques like supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to enhance its performance. The model achieves top scores on various benchmarks, outperforming traditional pipeline methods and demonstrating its effectiveness in end-to-end document parsing. Its robust performance across diverse scenarios showcases its ability to generalize well to different types of documents.

papers.title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable,Navigable, and Editable
papers.abstract: Abstract  The capability of a modern AI agent depends not only on its foundation model but also on its harness, which constructs prompts, manages state, invokes tools, and coordinates execution. As models, APIs, environments, and requirements evolve, the harness must be continually modified. Before such a change can be made, a developer or coding agent must identify all code locations that implement the target behavior. This is difficult because production harnesses are large, tightly coupled, and behaviorally distributed, while modification requests describe what the system should do and repositories are organized by files and modules. Code search, repository indexing, and long-context processing ease inspection, but still leave this behavior-to-code mapping to be recovered by hand. Behavior localization is therefore a central bottleneck in harness evolution. We introduce the Harness Handbook, a behavior-centric representation synthesized automatically from a harness codebase via static analysis and LLM-assisted structuring, linking each behavior to its corresponding source. We also introduce Behavior-Guided Progressive Disclosure (BGPD), which guides agents from high-level behaviors to relevant implementation details and verifies candidate locations against the current source. On diverse modification requests from two open-source harnesses, Handbook-Assisted planning improves behavior localization and edit-plan quality while using fewer planner tokens, with the largest gains on scattered sites, rarely executed paths, and cross-module interactions. Evolving complex agentic systems thus depends not only on generating edits, but also on determining where those edits should be made.

ru.title: Эволюция AI-агентов: от поведения к реализации
ru.desc: Статья рассматривает важность эволюции инструментов для современных AI-агентов, включающих фреймворки и модели. Для правильно управления поведением системы необходимо выявить все места в коде, которые реализуют цель поведения, что является сложной задачей из-за большой связанности и распределенности кода. Вводится 'Harness Handbook' — представление, автоматизированное с помощью статического анализа и LLM, которое связывает поведение с его источниками. Также предлагается метод BGPD, который направляет разработчиков от высокоуровневого поведения к деталям реализации.

en.title: Streamlining AI Harness Evolution with Behavior-Centric Tools
en.desc: This paper discusses the importance of a harness in AI systems, which manages prompts and execution as models and requirements change. It highlights the challenge of locating code that implements specific behaviors in large and complex codebases. The authors introduce the Harness Handbook, a tool that uses static analysis and LLMs to link behaviors to their source code. Additionally, they present Behavior-Guided Progressive Disclosure (BGPD) to help developers navigate from high-level behaviors to implementation details, improving the efficiency of code modifications.
